items.title: Localisations of a Noetherian Zariski pair at elements of the ideal are Jacobson rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that localising a Noetherian Zariski pair at an element of its ideal produces a Jacobson ring. The proof uses the dimension one criterion for Jacobson rings: given a prime of the localisation which is not maximal, the author reduces to the case of a domain in which the localisation has positive dimension, finds a nonzero prime not containing the chosen element, extends it to a maximal ideal, and uses the Zariski pair property to put the element's ideal inside that maximal ideal. The two primes are then distinct and the local ring at the maximal ideal has dimension at least two, so the spectrum of the localisation is infinite by the standard result on opens of spectra of two-dimensional Noetherian local domains, which is exactly what the criterion asks for.
